content.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret is not set — the Play Developer API service-account JSON key is required"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          echo "All required Android secrets are present"

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@651ff0d62c5c79bed6d53ec518387aae20e72c1a # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # gh-1468: same seed as ci.yml build-android — the release lane runs
      # the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download and rides the same
      # release-asset CDN roulette without it.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # release lane's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the lane. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # The lane wraps `flutter build appbundle --release`; the upload
      # keystore rides the ANDROID_* env vars (issue #289) and is decoded
      # by app/build.gradle.kts into the (gitignored) build dir — no
      # key.properties dance. ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING makes a
      # secret-less release build fail LOUDLY instead of debug-signing.
      - name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: the AAB's versionName rides the derived tag version
          # (BUILD_NAME) — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns. BUILD_NUMBER stays the run number
          # (Play versionCode).
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

  submit-android:
    name: Submit Android to Play
    needs: [build-android]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): supply
    # upload historically ~5m.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: needs.build-android.result == 'success'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Download AAB artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/aab/

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@651ff0d62c5c79bed6d53ec518387aae20e72c1a # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # Mirrors submit-ios: without the Play service account the upload
      # skips neutrally (the AAB stays on the GitHub release / artifacts).
      # Track policy (issue #289): manual dispatches default to the
      # internal track; the daily Play leg passes beta (external/open
      # testing). PLAY_VALIDATE_ONLY=1 flips the lane into a dry run.
      - name: Upload AAB to Google Play
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
          PLAY_TRACK: ${{ inputs.android_track }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play service account not configured — skipping the Play upload (the AAB stays on the GitHub release / artifacts)."
            exit 0
          fi
          AAB_PATH="$(find "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/flutter_app/aab" -name '*.aab' -type f | head -1)"
          echo "Uploading $AAB_PATH to the Play '$PLAY_TRACK' track..."
          ANDROID_AAB_PATH="$AAB_PATH" bundle exec fastlane android upload_only

      # Issue #947: android_content=all means the LISTING ships too. The
      # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device type
      # (supply appends, which is how a stale rejected screenshot survived
      # on the live listing) and verifies the committed state via
      # edits.images.list. Runs after the AAB upload so a release train
      # never ships a binary against a stale listing.
      - name: Deploy Play listing (metadata + images)
        if: inputs.android_content == 'all'
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
          PLAY_TRACK: ${{ inputs.android_track }}
          PLAY_DEPLOY_METADATA: 'true'
          PLAY_DEPLOY_IMAGES: 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play service account not configured — skipping the listing deploy."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "Deploying the Play listing (texts + images)..."
          bundle exec fastlane android play_store

  build-android-apks:
    # Issue #622: the flavor matrix. The AAB job above stays the Play
    # pipeline (store, unchanged); this job builds BOTH release APKs from
    # ONE variable — FLAVOR drives both the gradle --flavor and the
    # FA_FLAVOR dart-define (contract: the pair must never drift). god
    # (applicationId dev.fa1.app.god) is sideload-only and NEVER reaches
    # Play (binding threat model): it ships as an APK attached to the
    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets
    # an APK for direct installs + the UT-CI-1 size-delta tracking.
    name: Build Android APK (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services
      # plugin ("No matching client found for package name
      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder
      # google-services.json, which carries both clients.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"
          elif [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      # gh-1468: same seed as the ci.yml/ci AAB jobs — the flavor matrix
      # runs the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download per leg.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # flavor matrix's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the leg. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # Same release keystore as the AAB job (contract: store and god sign
      # with the SAME release key — only the applicationId differs), same
      # strict-signing posture: no silent debug-signed APKs. No Play
      # service account here — god never touches Play.
      - name: Build flavor APK
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: stamp the APK version strings from the derived tag
          # version — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns.
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        # ONE variable ($FLAVOR, job-level env from the matrix) feeds BOTH
        # the gradle flavor and the FA_FLAVOR dart-define.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          flutter build apk --release --flavor "$FLAVOR" --dart-define=FA_FLAVOR="$FLAVOR" \
            --build-name="$BUILD_NAME" --build-number="$BUILD_NUMBER"

      - name: Verify flavor APK
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          APK=$(find flutter_app/build/app/outputs -name "app-$FLAVOR-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$APK" ]; then
            echo "::error::app-$FLAVOR-release.apk not found under flutter_app/build/app/outputs"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "APK built successfully: $(ls -la "$APK")"

      - name: Store APK size delta vs previous release (UT-CI-1)
        if: matrix.flavor == 'store'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          APK=$(find flutter_app/build/app/outputs -name "app-store-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$APK")
          echo "store APK size: $SIZE bytes"
          # UT-CI-1: track the store APK size delta against the previous
          # release's app-store-release.apk asset. Threshold policy: FAIL
          # the job when the APK grows more than +10% release-over-release
          # (engine/asset bloat must be a conscious, changelogged
          # decision). The enforcement guard stays commented out until the
          # first flavor release exists to diff against — flip it on then.
          PREV_SIZE=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq '[.[].assets[] | select(.name == "app-store-release.apk")][0].size // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ -n "$PREV_SIZE" ]; then
            DELTA=$(python3 -c "print(f'{($SIZE - $PREV_SIZE) / $PREV_SIZE * 100:.1f}')")
            echo "Previous release store APK: $PREV_SIZE bytes — delta: ${DELTA}%"
            {
              echo '### Store APK size (UT-CI-1)'
              echo "- this release: $SIZE bytes"
              echo "- previous release: $PREV_SIZE bytes"
              echo "- delta: ${DELTA}% (fail threshold: +10%)"
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "No previous release store APK found — baseline recorded (this run: $SIZE bytes)."
          fi
          # UT-CI-1 enforcement (enable once a baseline exists):
          # if [ -n "$DELTA" ] && python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(0 if float('$DELTA') > 10.0 else 1)"; then
          #   echo "::error::store APK grew ${DELTA}% vs the previous release (UT-CI-1 threshold +10%)"
          #   exit 1
          # fi

      - name: Upload APK Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-${{ matrix.flavor }}
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-${{ matrix.flavor }}-release.apk
          retention-days: 14

  test-android-emulator:
    # Issue #622 (card DoD): emulator CI job shape for the six mobile
    # channel integration tests (flutter_app/test/integration/
    # mobile_channel_it.dart, tagged `integration`):
    #   IT-flavor-1  — release-manifest audit per flavor
    #   IT-floor-1   — mobile.* availability per tier (issue #19 floor)
    #   IT-observe-1 — hierarchy + screenshot over the channel
    #   IT-gesture-1 — tap / swipe / text injection
    #   IT-shell-1   — Shizuku round-trip (god + opt-in bridge)
    #   IT-consent-1 — consent flow + one-tap disable
    # DISABLED with `if: false` until an emulator runner is provisioned —
    # the hosted pool does not guarantee KVM and a red matrix would gate
    # every release. When provisioned: add
    # `needs: [version, build-android-apks]`, flip the `if` below to
    # `needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'`, add a
    # download-artifact step for `android-apk-${{ matrix.flavor }}` before
    # the emulator boot, and the job goes green as-is. The same ONE-var
    # rule applies: FLAVOR drives --flavor and FA_FLAVOR.
    name: Android emulator ITs (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: false
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Boot emulator
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test -e /dev/kvm || { echo "::error::/dev/kvm missing — the provisioned runner must expose KVM"; exit 1; }
          echo no | "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/avdmanager" create avd \
            -n fa-it --package "system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64" --device pixel_5
          "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -avd fa-it \
            -no-window -no-audio -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot -accel on &
          adb wait-for-device
          until [ "$(adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')" = "1" ]; do
            sleep 5
          done
          echo "Emulator booted"

      - name: Install flavor APK
        run: adb install -r "flutter_app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-$FLAVOR-release.apk"

      - name: Run mobile channel IT suite
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test test/integration/mobile_channel_it.dart --tags integration

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    # gh-1600 F-A + gh-1692: pin the ONE self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1)
    # via its unique registration label PLUS its runner-name label. The old
    # generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64] list also matched the Linux
    # self-hosted box's labels, and this job ran on Linux (`bundle: command
    # not found`, exit 127; later steps died on `security: command not
    # found`). `macos-m5` alone was still a coin flip: it matches BOTH
    # fa-m5-1 (proven good 10-16) AND fa-m5-2 (10-17/10-18 `** ARCHIVE
    # FAILED **`, signing env unverified) — the runner-name label `fa-m5-1`
    # resolves the job to the known-good box until fa-m5-2 is fixed.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

      # gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on this persistent box is SHARED across
      # workflow runs — the old bare workspace rm -rf failed the checkout on
      # stale unremovable bench leftovers
      # (jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/, docker-held trial mounts). Log-and-prune:
      # remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into
      # RUNNER_TEMP, and clone around a surviving mount stub — a stale
      # unremovable path can never fail the checkout. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          # gh-1692 AC3: the depth-1 clone pulls tip blobs from origin over
          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1692 AC2: the iOS lane pins xcbeautify as the xcodebuild
      # formatter (xcpretty "can result in missing some build errors" —
      # the 10-17/10-18 archive failures printed NO error line). Homebrew
      # keeps it a one-time install on this persistent runner; the step
      # verifies the binary so a missing formatter can never silently
      # re-introduce the xcpretty class.
      - name: Install xcbeautify (xcodebuild formatter, gh-1692)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v xcbeautify >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "xcbeautify already installed: $(xcbeautify --version)"
          else
            brew install xcbeautify
          fi
          xcbeautify --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no
      # retry. The bounded retry + deterministic-skew fail-fast now lives
      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in
      # the repo rides (gh-1310; pinned by test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
      # test.dart).
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # NOTE: no percent-decoding of the file: URI — pub-cache paths on
          # this runner carry no URI escapes; add unquoting if that changes.
          JS_WR=$(python3 -c '
            import json, pathlib
            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
            p = next((q for q in cfg["packages"] if q["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"), None)
            print(p["rootUri"] if p else "")
          ')
          if [ -z "$JS_WR" ]; then
            echo "::warning::js_widget_runtime not in package_config.json — no fixture to prune, skipping"
            exit 0
          fi
          case "$JS_WR" in
            file://*) JS_WR=${JS_WR#file://} ;;
          esac
          case "$JS_WR" in
            /*) ;;
            *) JS_WR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$JS_WR" ;;
          esac
          GLB="$JS_WR/test/assets/coach_anny.glb"
          if [ -f "$GLB" ]; then
            rm -f "$GLB"
            echo "pruned coach_anny.glb (5.6 MB never-loaded test fixture, #1331) from $JS_WR"
          else
            echo "coach_anny.glb already absent — nothing to prune"
          fi

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on

  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block

  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in

  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-succe…

blocks.text:
# ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 250m = child worst-case 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351; gh-1477 moved the version ceiling
          # 10 → 20m — blobless fetch + seatbelt) + 20m margin — a healthy
          # slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 15000 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
