#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in

    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"

title_select=""

dispatch() {

    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0

    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)

      android_track:

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

Now TDD RED: write the reproduction test. I need to:

1. Extend the gh stub to answer `gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq ...` polls from a `jobs-<id>.txt` fixture (one running-count per line, last line repeats; default "1" when absent so existing tests are unaffected).
2. Add tests:
  - RED repro (gh-172): attempt 1 run in_progress but 0 running jobs → stall → cancel + re-dispatch; attempt 2 same → fail fast with 'runner pool suspect', names run 222, and CANCELS 222 (containment).
  - Positive control: a transient queued gap (jobs go 0 → 1) does NOT trip the guard; run completes success.

Let me look at the existing test file structure for where to add — the #34 group (lines ~362-450). Let me view the exact region around the self-heal tests to place the new tests and check the stub `view` branch to mirror the pattern for a `jobs` fixture.

The stub `view` branch currently:
``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/canceled-\$id" ]; then
         status=completed; conclusion=cancelled
       else
         f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
         line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
         sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
         if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
         status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
       fi
       printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
       ;;
``

The script calls `gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion --jq ...`. With `--json jobs`, sub=$2... wait: `cmd="run"; sub="view"`, then `id="$3"` — for `gh run view 111 --repo ... --json jobs --jq ...`, $3=111 too. So the same branch handles it; I need to distinguish by whether "--json jobs" is in args. The stub already collects args into an array and finds --jq. I'll add: if args contain `--json` followed by `jobs`, then serve from jobs-<id>.txt with the same consume-a-line pattern, defaulting to "1" if no file; emit `{"jobs":[{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"queued"}]}`-ish... simplest: emit N in_progress jobs: running count N → `{"jobs":[...N×{"status":"in_progress"}]}`. jq in script: `[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length` → returns N.

Careful with the `cancelled-<id>` marker for the jobs call: after cancel, script has already left the loop; but for cleanliness, serve 0 running jobs when cancelled marker exists (a cancelled run has no running jobs). Actually for the containment test I assert `run cancel 222` in the log — after exit the script doesn't poll again. Fine either way; I'll still make cancelled → 0.

Implementation of the stub branch (careful escaping in the Dart raw string — the stub is inside a Dart string literal with \$ escapes):

``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       is_jobs=0
       for ((j=0; j<\${#args[@]}; j++)); do
         if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ] && [ "\${args[\$((j+1))]}" = "jobs" ]; then is_jobs=1; fi
       done
       if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
         if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/canceled-\$id" ]; then n=0
         else
           jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
           if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
             n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
             sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
             if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
           else
             n=1
           fi
         fi
         seq_out="[\`" -- hmm, build array of N in_progress
``

Building the JSON for N jobs in bash: 
``
json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"
printf '{"jobs":%s}' "$json" | apply_jq
``
Note: inside the Dart string, `\$` etc. Also `seq` could do: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n"`... seq with -s puts separator between. `seq -s, 1 0` gives... for n=0, `seq 1 0` outputs nothing → json="[]" — but with the -f format: `seq -f ... -s, 1 0` → empty. That's compact:
``
body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)
printf '{"jobs":[%s]}' "\$body" | apply_jq
``
seq -s, 1 3 → `{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"}`. For n=0 → empty → `[]`. 

Now the new tests. Also keep `view-111.txt` etc. The repro test:

```dart
test(
 'gh-172: a pool-held child (alive but nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, then fails fast and cancels the orphan',
 () {
   final dw = runDw(
     'queue-stall',
     [
       'build-mobile.yml',
       '--title',
       testflightTitle,
       '--budget-seconds',
       '600', // big: ONLY the queue-stall guard can end attempt 1
       '-f',
       'ios_content=all',
     ],
     {
       'runs.json': runJson([run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10))]),
       'runs2.json': runJson([
         run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10)),
         run(222, testflightTitle, iso(-1)),
       ]),
       'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       'view-222.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       // version done, build-ios queued forever: nothing in_progress.
       'jobs-111.txt': '0\n',
       'jobs-222.txt': '0\n',
     },
     env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '1', 'DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS': '1'},
   );
   expect(dw.exitCode, 1);
   expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 2);
   expect(dw.out, contains('runner pool suspect'));
   expect(dw.out, contains('222'));
   expect(
     dw.log.any((l) => l.contains('run cancel 222 --repo OWNER/REPO')),
     reason: 'the orphaned second run must be cancelled before the fail-fast exit',
   );
   expect(dw.out, contains('no running job') /* the stall signature */);
 },
);
``

Wait — one wrinkle: in runDw, DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS default is already '1'. And DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 → tight spin loop; the stall window (1s) fires after ~1s of polls. OK. But note the stall guard must consume polls — with sleep 0 the loop spins hot for 1s; that's fine (existing budget test with budget 1 does the same).

Positive control:

```dart
test('a transient queued gap (job pickup) does not trip the stall guard', () {
 final dw = runDw(
   'queue-transient',
   ['build-mobile.yml', '--title', playTitle, '--budget-seconds', '600', '-f', 'android_content=all'],
   {
     'runs.json': runJson([run(111, playTitle, iso(-10))]),
     // One poll sees nothing running (between version and build-ios),
     // then build-ios is running, then the run completes.
     'jobs-111.txt': '0\n1\n',
     'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n',
   },
   env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '2'},
 );
 expect(dw.exitCode, 0);
 expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 1);
});
``

Hmm — timing: with poll 0, polls happen as fast as gh stub runs (~few ms each). view-111 consumes line 1 (in_progress), jobs consumes '0' → last_progress=t0; next polls: view consumes 'in_progress' again... wait, the second view poll consumes line 2 of view-111 = 'in_progress -'. Then line exhausted → repeat last = 'completed success'?? No — re-read the stub: it takes head -1, deletes it, and if the file becomes empty it rewrites the consumed line. So the file shrinks to the last line and repeats it forever. view-111.txt 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n': poll1→in_progress, poll2→in_progress, poll3→completed success (file then holds just that line). jobs-111 '0\n1\n': poll1→0, poll2→1, poll3+→1 forever.

Sequence: p1: view=in_progress, jobs=0 → last_progress=t0 (initialize last_progress at loop start anyway). p2: view=in_progress, jobs=1 → refresh t1. p3: view=completed success → break. Exit 0 with one dispatch. The stall check at p2: now-t0 ≈ ms < 2s. Safe. But what if p1→p2 takes < stall and p2=1 refreshes — yes safe. To make it a REAL test of the guard, the gap must below the window: with DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2 and the '0' gap lasting ~ms, fine.

Hmm, but also I want a test that the stall guard on attempt 1 leads to re-dispatch (self-heal), not immediate failure — covered by the gh-172 test (it asserts 2 dispatches: attempt 1 stalled → re-dispatch → attempt 2 stalled → fail fast).

# ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the

blocks.text:
# ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 250m = child worst-case 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351; gh-1477 moved the version ceiling
          # 10 → 20m — blobless fetch + seatbelt) + 20m margin — a healthy
          # slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 15000 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

The timeline:

- If run #1 doesn't complete within 250m: cancel, wait up to 3m for cancel to land, re-dispatch at ~253m.
- Run #2 watches from ~253m. Budget is ANOTHER 250m. If run #2 also unfinished: watcher would exit at ~503m with the "SECOND attempt" error. But leg timeout is 360m, so the leg is killed at 360m — mid-watch of run #2, at ~107m into run #2's watch.

The leg was killed after 6h0m15s = at the ceiling. So this is consistent with: run #1 wedged/was slow → cancelled at 250m → re-dispatched run #2 → leg killed at 360m while watching run #2.

But wait — is that what actually happened? Let me check the actual run's log. The ticket says "(no failed-step log available — see the run link)". I can try `gh run view` from this environment. Let me check if gh is authenticated.

Actually, wait. Let me think about what else could hold the leg at 360m with no second wedge. The watcher polls `gh run view` every 60s. Hmm.

Actually, there's another important subtlety: the run list `find_run_id` — the appear window. But that's bounded at 600s.

Let me think about the deeper question: what should the fix be? The auto-filed ticket says "corelate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect". So first I should investigate the actual child run to see what happened.

Key question: was the child run wedged (then the self-heal worked as designed but the second wedge exceeded the leg ceiling — expected bounded behavior, though the leg goes red and auto-files an issue), or is there an actual bug in the watcher script that made it hang longer than the budget?

Hmm, actually, let me look more carefully. There's a potential bug in the watcher: after the FIRST wedge (cancel + re-dispatch), the watcher's SECOND attempt can run up to 250m more, totaling >360m, which exceeds the leg timeout. The daily-publish.yml comment says this is known and accepted ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast").

But hold on — is the leg timeout really the binding constraint here? Let me reconsider: could the FIRST attempt have legitimately run 250m without a wedge? The child worst-case is 230m. TestFlight submit can take longer... The build-mobile.yml jobs: version 20m → build-ios 90m → submit-ios 120m. That's 230m worst-case. The budget 250m gives only 20m margin. If the child legitimately exceeded 230m (e.g., Apple processing slow + queue time), the watcher would cancel a HEALTHY child mid-submit! Then the re-dispatched run #2 would run again, and at 360m the leg dies mid-watch of run #2. The leg fails (timeout = cancelled), and the run #2 might actually complete successfully later — but the leg already failed.

So possible root causes:
1. Child run genuinely wedged (e.g., self-hosted runner slot lost) → first-wedge self-heal at 250m → second attempt runs → leg timeout at 360m bounds it. The auto-filed issue is "working as designed" in the sense the system bounded the damage, but the leg still goes red.
2. Child run was healthy but slow (exceeded 230m worst-case legitimately) → watcher cancelled a healthy child (violating the #351 invariant) → re-dispatch → leg timeout at 360m. This IS a defect: budget too tight.
3. Some watcher bug (e.g., `gh` hanging, sleep drift) kept the leg busy without progress.

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:

    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"

body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
