blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477: 10m
    # was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew it and cancelled the
    # job mid-fetch (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

Interesting! Child #1:
- Build iOS IPA: started 05:28:04, cancelled 09:38:29 — ran 4h10m25s! That job was supposed to have `timeout-minutes: 90`. But it ran 250 minutes! The job-level timeout DID NOT fire at 90m!

Wait — the comment says "Issue #34: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report) otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers." with timeout-minutes: 90.

But the job ran 4h10m — from 05:28:04 to 09:38:29 — and its conclusion is "cancelled" (by the watcher's `gh run cancel` at ~09:38), NOT "cancelled by job timeout at 90m". So the job-level timeout-minutes: 90 did NOT fire on this self-hosted runner!

Hmm, actually wait. Let me reconsider: Job timeouts on self-hosted runners require the runner to process the cancellation... Actually no — job-level timeouts are enforced by the RUNER process (the Runner.Listener/Worker enforces the job timeout via a timer and cancels the steps). On self-hosted runners, the timeout IS enforced by the runner worker. But there's a known issue: if the worker process is hung (e.g., blocked on a step process that ignores SIGINT/SIGTERM... the worker escalates to SIGKILL eventually), the timeout processing can be delayed. There are documented cases where the job-level timeout on self-hosted runners doesn't fire when the worker is stuck in a syscall (e.g., waiting on a child process that captured the job's stdio). 

Actually more importantly: was the build-ios job making progress or wedged? It ran 4h10m — far beyond its 90m ceiling. The job should have been killed at 90m (07:00-ish) by the job timeout, freeing the runner. Instead it kept the slot until the watcher cancelled the RUN at 09:38 (the run cancel marked the job cancelled server-side at 09:38:29).

And then — CRITICAL — after the run-cancel at 09:38:30, child #2's build-ios job went to `queued` at 09:40:18 and is STILL queued NOW (12:01 UTC — over 2h20m later!). This means the self-hosted runner fa-m5-1 NEVER picked up the new job — i.e., the runner-side worker is STILL stuck processing the cancelled build-ios job of child #1. The server-side run cancel marked everything cancelled in the API, but the physical runner box is still occupied by the wedged worker process, so it can't take the new job. This is exactly issue #34's scenario: "a wedged self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report holds a job in_progress forever, blocking the single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their timeout".

Hmm wait, but let me double check: is fa-m5-1 perhaps offline entirely? If the runner process itself died (machine rebooted, runner stopped), the job would also stay queued forever. Either way — the runner can't take the job.

Let me check the runner status via the API: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runers to see if fa-m5-1 is online/busy.

Also let me look at what the build-ios job of child #1 was doing when it wedged — check its logs/steps. `gh run view --log` for the job. The job id — let me get it.

Also, worth noting: the "Submit iOS to TestFlight" and "Create Mobile GitHub Release" jobs of child #1 show startedAt 09:38:30 with conclusion cancelled — those are artifacts of the run cancellation (they were "started" at cancel time because needs dependency? Odd but not important).

Now, what's the actual BUG here — the thing a product-code fix should address?

The ticket is auto-filed by the daily pipeline. The leg failed because:
1. Child #1's build-ios job exceeded its 90m job timeout (ran 250m) — the job-level timeout did not bound it (or the worker was wedged in a way that timeout processing couldn't cancel the steps).
2. The watcher cancelled child #1 at the 250m budget and re-dispatched child #2 (working as designed).
3. Child #2's build-ios queued forever because the runner was still occupied by the wedged worker from child #1 (the cancel of the RUN doesn't free the runner if the worker is wedged; the runner-side worker never acknowledged).
4. The leg hit its 360m ceiling while child #2's iOS job sat queued.

So the root cause: a single physical self-hosted macOS runner (fa-m5-1) with a wedged/stuck worker — cancellation of the run frees the slot in GitHub's database but NOT on the physical box; the re-dispatch then queues behind the zombie, and the leg dies at its timeout ceiling.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"

Can't list runners with this token. But the evidence is already strong:

1. Child #1's `Build iOS IPA` job ran 05:28:04 → 09:38:29 (250m!) despite `timeout-minutes: 90`. It was cancelled only by the WATCHER's `gh run cancel` at the 250m budget.
2. The re-dispatched child #2's `Build iOS IPA` has been `queued` since 09:40:18 — now >2h20m — meaning the physical runner (fa-m5-1) never came back to take the job. The server-side cancel marked the run/jobs cancelled in the API, but the runner-side worker never processed the cancellation / never reported completion, so the single-runner pool is still occupied.

This is EXACTLY the #34 class: "a wedged self-hosted runner ... holds the slot ... blocking the single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their timeout."

Now: what does the current watcher do wrong, and what's the minimal targeted fix?

Current watcher behavior for the testflight leg:
- Watch run #1 for 250m → still unfinished → cancel + re-dispatch run #2.
- Watch run #2 for another 250m (budget is per-atempt, not global!). The leg ceiling is 360m; watching run #2 from t≈253m means the leg dies at t=360m mid-watch, ~107m into run #2's watch, with no diagnostic and — crucialy — WITHOUT cancelling run #2, leaving the queued child running/orphaned after the leg is dead.

Wait, actually there's an important subtlety: when the leg job is killed at the 360m timeout, the child run #2 continues (GitHub doesn't cancel the child when the parent leg dies). Run #2 is queued forever → it will sit there until... hmm, actually run #2 is STILL queued right now. It will apparently never start (runner wedged), so it'll queue forever unless manually cancelled. There's a "Sweep stale release drafts" job but no stale-run sweper.

So the defects to fix, in order of impact:

**Defect A (the wedge itself):** the self-hosted runner fa-m5-1 got wedged mid-build (the 90m job timeout did not bound it — the job ran 250m; the worker apparently stopped communicating with the server: no steps logged...). Actually wait — can I really conclude the timeout didn't fire? Let me think again. timeout-minutes: 90 on the job. Job started 05:28:04. 90m → 06:58. The job kept going until 09:38:29 (cancelled by watcher). So yes — the job-level timeout did NOT fire. Why? 

Known GitHub issue: on self-hosted runners, if the worker process is stuck in a way that it can't process the cancellation message (e.g., the machine's clock, or the runner process crashed while the machine kept running), the server can't enforce job timeout for self-hosted runners — job timeouts are enforced BY THE RUNER, not by the server. For GitHub-hosted runners, the service enforces them server-side. For self-hosted, "The timeout is enforced by the runner itself" — if the runner/worker is unresponsive, no enforcement happens. Actually hmm, I recall: GitHub docs say job timeouts apply to self-hosted runners too, but there are many reports of self-hosted jobs exceeding timeout when the runner is hung. The enforcement mechanism: Runner.Listener → Worker process sets a timer; if the worker is hung hard (deadlocked in native code, disk I/O hang), it can't self-cancel.

So the wedged worker ALSO explains why the run cancel didn't free the box: the cancel is processed by the same hung worker → never processed → the runner never says "job done" → the runner stays "busy" in GitHub's scheduler → child #2's iOS job queues forever.

**Defect B (watcher gap):** the watcher treats "run status == in_progress/queued" as progress. After the self-heal re-dispatch, it watches run #2 for another full budget, but the leg ceiling (360m) kills everything mid-watch with zero diagnostics and orphans run #2. The #351 arithmetic already acknowledges testflight cannot fit two full budgets under 360m. The watcher has no leg-budget awareness: it should take the LEG ceiling into account and fail fast (with diagnostics naming the queued run + suspected runner) before the ceiling eats the leg silently.

So the minimum targeted fix in-repo (this is what we can fix; the wedged physical box itself is ops):

1. **`dispatch_and_watch.sh`: make the budget GLOBAL across attempts, not per-atempt.** I.e., the watcher's total watch time across cancel+re-dispatch must fit inside the leg ceiling; the second attempt gets the REMAING budget (leg ceiling − elapsed − margin), and — key improvement — **fail fast with a diagnostic when the re-dispatched run shows a queued job on a busy runner** rather than burning the remaining leg time watching a queued job that can never start.

2. Specifically for the observed failure mode: after re-dispatch, the child never starts its critical job (stays queued) because the runner pool is still held by the zombie worker. The watcher should detect "child run's jobs are all queued/skipped for > N minutes after appear" (i.e., no job actually running) and fail fast with an actionable error naming the runner suspicion — instead of silently timing out at the leg ceiling.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

  started=$(date +%s)

  while :; do

**Defect 1 — the self-heal re-dispatches without checking the pool is actually free.** `gh run cancel` succeeded server-side (run #1 marked cancelled), but the physical runner never acknowledged. The watcher immediately re-dispatches, and the new child queues behind the zombie forever. The watcher then burns the remaining leg time watching a queued run that can never start.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

Now TDD RED: write the reproduction test. I need to:

1. Extend the gh stub to answer `gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq ...` polls from a `jobs-<id>.txt` fixture (one running-count per line, last line repeats; default "1" when absent so existing tests are unaffected).
2. Add tests:
  - RED repro (gh-172): attempt 1 run in_progress but 0 running jobs → stall → cancel + re-dispatch; attempt 2 same → fail fast with 'runner pool suspect', names run 222, and CANCELS 222 (containment).
  - Positive control: a transient queued gap (jobs go 0 → 1) does NOT trip the guard; run completes success.

Let me look at the existing test file structure for where to add — the #34 group (lines ~362-450). Let me view the exact region around the self-heal tests to place the new tests and check the stub `view` branch to mirror the pattern for a `jobs` fixture.

The stub `view` branch currently:
``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/canceled-\$id" ]; then
         status=completed; conclusion=cancelled
       else
         f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
         line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
         sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
         if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
         status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
       fi
       printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
       ;;
``

The script calls `gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion --jq ...`. With `--json jobs`, sub=$2... wait: `cmd="run"; sub="view"`, then `id="$3"` — for `gh run view 111 --repo ... --json jobs --jq ...`, $3=111 too. So the same branch handles it; I need to distinguish by whether "--json jobs" is in args. The stub already collects args into an array and finds --jq. I'll add: if args contain `--json` followed by `jobs`, then serve from jobs-<id>.txt with the same consume-a-line pattern, defaulting to "1" if no file; emit `{"jobs":[{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"queued"}]}`-ish... simplest: emit N in_progress jobs: running count N → `{"jobs":[...N×{"status":"in_progress"}]}`. jq in script: `[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length` → returns N.

Careful with the `cancelled-<id>` marker for the jobs call: after cancel, script has already left the loop; but for cleanliness, serve 0 running jobs when cancelled marker exists (a cancelled run has no running jobs). Actually for the containment test I assert `run cancel 222` in the log — after exit the script doesn't poll again. Fine either way; I'll still make cancelled → 0.

Implementation of the stub branch (careful escaping in the Dart raw string — the stub is inside a Dart string literal with \$ escapes):

``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       is_jobs=0
       for ((j=0; j<\${#args[@]}; j++)); do
         if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ] && [ "\${args[\$((j+1))]}" = "jobs" ]; then is_jobs=1; fi
       done
       if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
         if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/canceled-\$id" ]; then n=0
         else
           jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
           if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
             n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
             sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
             if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
           else
             n=1
           fi
         fi
         seq_out="[\`" -- hmm, build array of N in_progress
``

Building the JSON for N jobs in bash: 
``
json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"
printf '{"jobs":%s}' "$json" | apply_jq
``
Note: inside the Dart string, `\$` etc. Also `seq` could do: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n"`... seq with -s puts separator between. `seq -s, 1 0` gives... for n=0, `seq 1 0` outputs nothing → json="[]" — but with the -f format: `seq -f ... -s, 1 0` → empty. That's compact:
``
body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)
printf '{"jobs":[%s]}' "\$body" | apply_jq
``
seq -s, 1 3 → `{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"}`. For n=0 → empty → `[]`. 

Now the new tests. Also keep `view-111.txt` etc. The repro test:

```dart
test(
 'gh-172: a pool-held child (alive but nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, then fails fast and cancels the orphan',
 () {
   final dw = runDw(
     'queue-stall',
     [
       'build-mobile.yml',
       '--title',
       testflightTitle,
       '--budget-seconds',
       '600', // big: ONLY the queue-stall guard can end attempt 1
       '-f',
       'ios_content=all',
     ],
     {
       'runs.json': runJson([run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10))]),
       'runs2.json': runJson([
         run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10)),
         run(222, testflightTitle, iso(-1)),
       ]),
       'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       'view-222.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       // version done, build-ios queued forever: nothing in_progress.
       'jobs-111.txt': '0\n',
       'jobs-222.txt': '0\n',
     },
     env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '1', 'DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS': '1'},
   );
   expect(dw.exitCode, 1);
   expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 2);
   expect(dw.out, contains('runner pool suspect'));
   expect(dw.out, contains('222'));
   expect(
     dw.log.any((l) => l.contains('run cancel 222 --repo OWNER/REPO')),
     reason: 'the orphaned second run must be cancelled before the fail-fast exit',
   );
   expect(dw.out, contains('no running job') /* the stall signature */);
 },
);
``

Wait — one wrinkle: in runDw, DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS default is already '1'. And DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 → tight spin loop; the stall window (1s) fires after ~1s of polls. OK. But note the stall guard must consume polls — with sleep 0 the loop spins hot for 1s; that's fine (existing budget test with budget 1 does the same).

Positive control:

```dart
test('a transient queued gap (job pickup) does not trip the stall guard', () {
 final dw = runDw(
   'queue-transient',
   ['build-mobile.yml', '--title', playTitle, '--budget-seconds', '600', '-f', 'android_content=all'],
   {
     'runs.json': runJson([run(111, playTitle, iso(-10))]),
     // One poll sees nothing running (between version and build-ios),
     // then build-ios is running, then the run completes.
     'jobs-111.txt': '0\n1\n',
     'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n',
   },
   env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '2'},
 );
 expect(dw.exitCode, 0);
 expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 1);
});
``

Hmm — timing: with poll 0, polls happen as fast as gh stub runs (~few ms each). view-111 consumes line 1 (in_progress), jobs consumes '0' → last_progress=t0; next polls: view consumes 'in_progress' again... wait, the second view poll consumes line 2 of view-111 = 'in_progress -'. Then line exhausted → repeat last = 'completed success'?? No — re-read the stub: it takes head -1, deletes it, and if the file becomes empty it rewrites the consumed line. So the file shrinks to the last line and repeats it forever. view-111.txt 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n': poll1→in_progress, poll2→in_progress, poll3→completed success (file then holds just that line). jobs-111 '0\n1\n': poll1→0, poll2→1, poll3+→1 forever.

Sequence: p1: view=in_progress, jobs=0 → last_progress=t0 (initialize last_progress at loop start anyway). p2: view=in_progress, jobs=1 → refresh t1. p3: view=completed success → break. Exit 0 with one dispatch. The stall check at p2: now-t0 ≈ ms < 2s. Safe. But what if p1→p2 takes < stall and p2=1 refreshes — yes safe. To make it a REAL test of the guard, the gap must below the window: with DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2 and the '0' gap lasting ~ms, fine.

Hmm, but also I want a test that the stall guard on attempt 1 leads to re-dispatch (self-heal), not immediate failure — covered by the gh-172 test (it asserts 2 dispatches: attempt 1 stalled → re-dispatch → attempt 2 stalled → fail fast).

Where to place: inside the same group as the self-heal tests (`#34 — wedge self-healing...` presumably). Let me read lines 340-362 to see the group header.

## Failure timeline (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20)

- 05:27:10 — `Leg: TestFlight` starts; dispatches build-mobile.yml ("build-mobile (none/all)").
- 05:27:18 — child #1 (run 39374977270) created. `Derive version` OK at 05:28:04. `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on fa-m5-1 (self-hosted).
- The build-ios job runs **250 minutes** — its own `timeout-minutes: 90` never fires (worker wedged/hung: no logs available, steps array empty — the worker stopped reporting). The run stays `in_progress`.
- 09:37-09:38 — watcher hits its 15000s (250m) budget → cancels run #1 (`gh run cancel`) → the API marks run #1 cancelled at 09:38:30. **But the physical worker never processes the cancel** (the same hung worker that ignored the 90m job timeout also can't process run cancellation) — the runner never frees.
- 09:39:31 — watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750). version OK 09:40:18; `Build iOS IPA` → **queued at 09:40:18, still queued right now (12:01 UTC, 2h21m later)** — the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool. The queued run will never start.
- 11:27:25 — leg hits its 360m ceiling; GitHub kills the watcher mid-`sleep`. No fail-fast diagnostic, no cleanup of the orphaned child #2. Leg marked cancelled → issue auto-filed (this ticket).

So: the *proximate* root cause is the wedged self-hosted worker (ops/infra), but the *fixable* defect in the repo is in the watcher's design, in two parts:

**Defect 1 — the self-heal re-dispatches without checking the pool is actually free.** `gh run cancel` succeeded server-side (run #1 marked cancelled), but the physical runner never acknowledged. The watcher immediately re-dispatches, and the new child queues behind the zombie forever. The watcher then burns the remaining leg time watching a queued run that can never start.

**Defect 2 — no queue-progress guard: a child whose jobs never START is treated identically to a healthy child making progress.** The budget loop only checks `status != completed` and wall-clock. A run sitting `queued` (or `in_progress` with the critical job queued) will consume the whole budget/leg ceiling. There's no "queued too long" detection. And when the leg ceiling finally kills the watcher, the orphaned child #2 is left queued forever (it's STILL queued 2.5h later), plus the auto-filed issue has no diagnostics ("no failed-step log available").

Hmm wait — but let me reconsider. Is the *right* fix per the #34/#351 design philosophy to make the watcher detect the zombie-pool case and fail fast? What CAN the watcher do about a zombie worker holding the pool? It cannot SSH into the runner. But it CAN:
1. Detect that the re-dispatched run's jobs are queued for an extended window (say 10-15m — hosted `version` job takes ~40s, then build-ios queues) → conclude the runner pool is still held → **fail fast** with an actionable error naming both runs and the suspected zombie runner, instead of silently eating the remaining ~107 minutes of leg time and dying as a bare ceiling timeout.
2. Cancel the orphaned run before failing so the queued zombie-child doesn't sit in the queue forever (and can't later start and double-publish against a future run — well, actually if it eventually starts it would build+publish a duplicate; cancelling is strictly correct on the failure path).

Also — what about the FIRST attempt? Could the watcher have detected the wedged build-ios job earlier than 250m? The job-level timeout-minutes: 90 SHOULD have fired at ~90m on the runner. It didn't (worker hung). Server-side, GitHub has no per-job timeout enforcement for self-hosted runners... wait, is that true? Let me think. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

Hmm — the RED failure exposes a fixture wrinkle: after attempt 1's cancel, attempt 2's dispatch "never appeared" — because the stub switches to runs2.json only once a `cancelled-*` marker exists AND... wait, it did cancel 111 (warning line shows the self-heal), so `cancelled-111` exists and runs2.json should serve. But the error says "run never appeared ... after 0s" — the appear window computed `appear_attempts * appear_poll` = 20 * 0 = 0s, and find_run_id returned 0 → hmm, "after 0s" message is right for poll=0. Why did find_run_id return nothing for run 222?

`find_run_id` floor: `epoch - 30`. runs2.json has run 222 at iso(-1) = 1s ago... and run 111 at iso(-10). floor = now-30 → both pass. Title matches. sort_by createdAt, .[-1] → 222. Should find it...

Unless `wait_for_run` wasn't even reached on attempt 2 — look at the sequence: after the budget fires (60s? no wait — the log shows the warning after "unfinished after 60s" — so budget path at 60s), cancel, cancel-wait loop (DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS=1 → one poll of `view 111` → stub: cancelled-111 exists → status=completed → break), attempt=2, continue 2 → dispatch again → find_run_id... 

The stub's run list branch: `if ls cancelled-* && [ -f runs2.json ] → runs_file=runs2.json` — should list 222. Hmm, but "GH_STUB_LIST_EMPTY_FIRST" not set... `calls` counter keeps incrementing; `calls -le 0` false → cat runs2.json | apply_jq with the script's jq expression... 

OH WAIT. I see it — the jq expression: `select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= floor)`. The stub pipes runs2.json through the REAL jq with the SCRIPT's expression — fine for old tests (self-heal test works). Why would 222 not be found here... createdAt=iso(-1) — computed when the FIXTURE was created. The stall test's attempt 1 consumed... hmm wait, no — the difference from the working self-heal test: my test has budget 60 with DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 — the watch loop SPINS HOT for 60 real seconds (sleep 0). During that time `iso(-1)`... the fixture was created at test start; attempt 2's dispatch happens ~61s later; `floor = epoch - 30` where epoch = attempt-2 dispatch time. Run 222's createdAt = testStart - 1s. floor = testStart + 61 - 30 = testStart + 31 > createdAt → run 222 is OLDER than the floor → excluded! THAT's why it never appeared.

The existing self-heal test (budget 1) doesn't hit this because attempt 2 happens ~1s after fixture creation, still inside the 30s window.

Fix the fixture: use iso(-10) for BOTH runs — no. The floor requires createdAt >= dispatchEpoch - 30. For attempt 2 at ~+61s, createdAt must be ≥ +31s... but createdAt is written at fixture creation (attempt-1 time). The stub serves runs2.json content as-is; I can make runs2.json's 222 entry createdAt iso(+70) (in the FUTURE — fine for the stub, it's just a string; fromdateiso8601 of a future timestamp > floor). But careful: attempt 2's find_run_id floor is epoch-30 where epoch≈+61; +70 ≥ +31 ✓. And sort_by(.createdAt) with only-222 visible... runs2.json includes 111 (iso(-10)) too: 111's createdAt -10 < floor +31 → excluded. Good: only 222 matches → latched.

Hmm wait, but does attempt 2's `wait_for_run` also then try `find_run_id` and get 222 — yes.

Alternatively reduce the hot-spin: use DW_POLL_SECONDS=1? Then budget 60 fires after ~60 poll-cycles × 1s ≈ 60s — same wall time. The hot spin with poll 0 burns CPU for 60s per attempt (two attempts = 120s of busy-loop + gh stub subprocess spawns — each poll spawns bash+gh+jq... poll 0 → as fast as possible — that's heavy: 60s × maybe 20-50 spawns/s). Actually the EXISTING double-wedge test uses budget 1 + poll 0 (~1s spin — fine). My budget-60 choice makes RED take ~2min of hot spinning. That's too slow AND caused this fixture wrinkle.

Better: shrink RED/GREEN cycle — budget 60 is only needed so GREEN's stall window (1s) beats it. What if I keep budget LARGE in GREEN via env override... no — simpler: DW_POLL_SECONDS stays 0, budget 60... the hot spin is the problem.

Hmm — actually can I make the budget path not wall-clock-bound in the test? The elapsed check is `[ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]`. No knob. OK alternatives:

1. budget 3: GREEN stall=1 fires at ~1s < 3 ✓ (margin 2s — poll cycle time vs 1s stall... each cycle = status gh call + jobs gh call + date + sleep 0 ≈ tens of ms; the stall check at ~1s fires safely before 3s budget). RED: budget 3 → attempt1 ~3s, attempt2 ~3s → exit ~7s total. Fixture window: attempt 2 at ~+7s → 222 createdAt iso(-1) still ≥ floor(-30+7=-23) ✓ — original iso(-1) works! And hot-spin only ~6s total. 

2. Keep 60 but give runs2.json a future createdAt — works but 120s of hot spin per test run is unacceptable.

Go with budget 3 for the pool-held test (update comment), and transient test budget 3 as well (it completes in ms; budget just needs to exceed the stall window 2s... transient stall window is DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2, budget 3: gap poll1 ~0ms, refresh at poll2 — fires never. fine).

Wait, also reconsider the transient test's window: with poll 0, polls are FAST (each ~5-20ms); stall window 2s means a '0' would have to persist 2s. Fixture '0\n1\n' → one poll at 0, next at 1 → never 2s. Good.

Also — the stub `gh` invocation log will be big from hot spins but fine.

Edge: with budget 3 and stall 1 in the pool-held test — attempt 1: watch starts, first polls: status in_progress, jobs 0 → last_progress=watchStart; at ~1s stall fires BEFORE budget 3 ✓. GREEN message 'no running job' + self-heal. Attempt 2 same → SECOND attempt fail with 'runner pool suspect' + cancel 222.

messages.preview: RED is clean: the old script rides the budget path, never detects the stall, never cancels the orphan run. Now GREEN — implement the queue-stall guard in the watcher:

blocks.text:
RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

Wait — careful with the second-atempt message shape. Existing test asserts out contains 'runner pool suspect' and '222' — my message keeps both ('runner pool suspect (issue #34)'). And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

3. Also worth documenting the knob in the usage/env comment block at the top of the script: `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600)`.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic. 

5. While in the yml — no changes to budgets/ceilings (the #351 table must stay in sync with the test).

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

Message wording — keep the signature phrase 'no running job' (test asserts it):
- warning (attempt 1): `::warning::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie) — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- error (attempt 2): `::error::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34, gh-172); URL`

Hmm — to avoid duplicating, keep the wedge string as the cause phrase: wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 zombie-pool signature)" and wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s". Then:
- attempt1: `::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- attempt2: `::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL`

Test asserts out contains 'no running job' ✓ and 'runner pool suspect' ✓.

Let me now write the script changes.
RED is clean: the old script rides the budget path, never detects the stall, never cancels the orphan run. Now GREEN — implement the queue-stall guard in the watcher:
