Now I have a very good picture of the existing test coverage and design. Let me now nail down the root cause and figure out the *minimum targeted fix*.

## Failure timeline (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20)

- 05:27:10 — `Leg: TestFlight` starts; dispatches build-mobile.yml ("build-mobile (none/all)").
- 05:27:18 — child #1 (run 39374977270) created. `Derive version` OK at 05:28:04. `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on fa-m5-1 (self-hosted).
- The build-ios job runs **250 minutes** — its own `timeout-minutes: 90` never fires (worker wedged/hung: no logs available, steps array empty — the worker stopped reporting). The run stays `in_progress`.
- 09:37-09:38 — watcher hits its 15000s (250m) budget → cancels run #1 (`gh run cancel`) → the API marks run #1 cancelled at 09:38:30. **But the physical worker never processes the cancel** (the same hung worker that ignored the 90m job timeout also can't process run cancellation) — the runner never frees.
- 09:39:31 — watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750). version OK 09:40:18; `Build iOS IPA` → **queued at 09:40:18, still queued right now (12:01 UTC, 2h21m later)** — the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool. The queued run will never start.
- 11:27:25 — leg hits its 360m ceiling; GitHub kills the watcher mid-`sleep`. No fail-fast diagnostic, no cleanup of the orphaned child #2. Leg marked cancelled → issue auto-filed (this ticket).

So: the *proximate* root cause is the wedged self-hosted worker (ops/infra), but the *fixable* defect in the repo is in the watcher's design, in two parts:

**Defect 1 — the self-heal re-dispatches without checking the pool is actually free.** `gh run cancel` succeeded server-side (run #1 marked cancelled), but the physical runner never acknowledged. The watcher immediately re-dispatches, and the new child queues behind the zombie forever. The watcher then burns the remaining leg time watching a queued run that can never start.

**Defect 2 — no queue-progress guard: a child whose jobs never START is treated identically to a healthy child making progress.** The budget loop only checks `status != completed` and wall-clock. A run sitting `queued` (or `in_progress` with the critical job queued) will consume the whole budget/leg ceiling. There's no "queued too long" detection. And when the leg ceiling finally kills the watcher, the orphaned child #2 is left queued forever (it's STILL queued 2.5h later), plus the auto-filed issue has no diagnostics ("no failed-step log available").

Hmm wait — but let me reconsider. Is the *right* fix per the #34/#351 design philosophy to make the watcher detect the zombie-pool case and fail fast? What CAN the watcher do about a zombie worker holding the pool? It cannot SSH into the runner. But it CAN:
1. Detect that the re-dispatched run's jobs are queued for an extended window (say 10-15m — hosted `version` job takes ~40s, then build-ios queues) → conclude the runner pool is still held → **fail fast** with an actionable error naming both runs and the suspected zombie runner, instead of silently eating the remaining ~107 minutes of leg time and dying as a bare ceiling timeout.
2. Cancel the orphaned run before failing so the queued zombie-child doesn't sit in the queue forever (and can't later start and double-publish against a future run — well, actually if it eventually starts it would build+publish a duplicate; cancelling is strictly correct on the failure path).

Also — what about the FIRST attempt? Could the watcher have detected the wedged build-ios job earlier than 250m? The job-level timeout-minutes: 90 SHOULD have fired at ~90m on the runner. It didn't (worker hung). Server-side, GitHub has no per-job timeout enforcement for self-hosted runners... wait, is that true? Let me think. Actually — job-level `timeout-minutes` IS enforced by the runner application. For self-hosted runners, if the runner process is healthy, the timeout fires. GitHub docs: "The timeout-minutes ... applies to each job ... The maximum is 360 minutes". There have been reports that self-hosted runners sometimes don't enforce it when the worker is stuck (exactly this bug class). We cannot fix GitHub's enforcement from the repo. BUT the watcher could add a **job-level progress check**: poll the run's jobs and detect "a job has been running longer than its known ceiling" or "the run is in_progress but no job has progressed in X minutes". That's a deeper change.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider: is there a cheaper, more targeted signal? In this specific failure:
- t+~90m: build-ios exceeded its 90m ceiling. The watcher polls `gh run view $run_id --json status,conclusion`. It could also poll jobs with `gh run view --json jobs` and check elapsed-vs-ceiling per job... but the watcher is shared across legs with different child workflows and different job ceilings; hard-coding ceilings per job into the shared script is heavy. But the LEG knows its budget: child worst-case 230m. The job ceiling approach would catch the wedge at ~90m instead of 250m — that saves ~160m of the 360m leg, leaving enough room for the re-dispatch to actually fit (230m child + margin ≈ 250m... 90m + 13m + 250m = 353m < 360m — just barely fits! Interesting — that's presumably exactly why the #351 comment says "leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg" — for testflight it does NOT fit (515m > 360m), which is why they accepted "a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast").

But hold on — that acceptance was about a SECOND WEDGE of the child run (watch budget expiring again). What actually happened here is worse and DIFFERENT: after the self-heal, the re-dispatched child NEVER STARTED (queued forever on the zombie-held pool). The watcher happily watched it for the remaining ~107m and the leg died at the ceiling with no diagnostics.

So the minimum targeted fix that addresses THIS failure's root cause within the watcher:

1. **Queue-start guard (the actual gap):** after a run appears, verify it actually STARTS running within a bounded window (the appear margin already exists — 60×10s=10m; but once correlated, the watcher goes straight into the status loop and never checks whether the run left `queued`). If the run (specifically: its non-skipped jobs) stays queued past a bounded window (say 10m — the same margin used elsewhere; a healthy child's `version` job starts within seconds), treat it as the #34 zombie-pool signature → cancel the orphan run (cleanup) → fail fast with an actionable `::error::` naming the queued run + runner-pool suspicion.

Actually wait — should the queue guard apply on attempt 1 too? Yes: it's the same class (run never starts). On attempt 1, "queued forever" could ALSO be a transient hosted-runner capacity event. 10m of zero-start on a child whose first job is ubuntu-latest `version` is strong evidence of a problem (version normally starts within seconds; even heavy load resolves in minutes). If we fail fast on attempt 1, we lose the possibility of a late start... but keeping the leg alive watching a queued run also just burns to the ceiling (that's exactly today's behavior — the ceiling kill produced a worse outcome: no diagnostics + orphaned run). Given the leg ceiling (360m) > budget (250m), a "queued too long" fail on attempt 1 at ~10m would leave ~340m unused — could we instead re-dispatch instead of failing? Careful: re-dispatching when the pool is zombie-held just queues another child (the pool stays held). The #34 fix chose "cancel + re-dispatch ONCE, then fail fast naming the pool". For the queue case the equivalent: on attempt 1, if the run never starts within the queue window → cancel it, re-dispatch once (the one self-heal); if the SECOND run also never starts → fail fast naming the pool. That keeps exactly one self-heal, symmetric with the in_progress wedge path, and always ends with a diagnostic + a cancelled orphan instead of a silent ceiling death.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

The script calls `gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion --jq ...`. With `--json jobs`, sub=$2... wait: `cmd="run"; sub="view"`, then `id="$3"` — for `gh run view 111 --repo ... --json jobs --jq ...`, $3=111 too. Careful with the `cancelled-<id>` marker for the jobs call: after cancel, script has already left the loop; but for cleanliness, serve 0 running jobs when cancelled marker exists (a cancelled run has no running jobs). Actually for the containment test I assert `run cancel 222` in the log — after exit the script doesn't poll again. Fine either way; I'll still make cancelled → 0.

``

Building the JSON for N jobs in bash: 
``
json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"
printf '{"jobs":%s}' "$json" | apply_jq
``
Note: inside the Dart string, `\$` etc. Also `seq` could do: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n"`... seq with -s puts separator between. `seq -s, 1 0` gives... for n=0, `seq 1 0` outputs nothing → json="[]" — but with the -f format: `seq -f ... -s, 1 0` → empty. That's compact:
``
body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)

seq -s, 1 3 → `{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"}`. For n=0 → empty → `[]`.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

1. Extend the gh stub to answer `gh run view <id> --json jobs --jq ...` polls from a `jobs-<id>.txt` fixture (one running-count per line, last line repeats; default "1" when absent so existing tests are unaffected).
2. Add tests:
  - RED repro (gh-172): attempt 1 run in_progress but 0 running jobs → stall → cancel + re-dispatch; attempt 2 same → fail fast with 'runner pool suspect', names run 222, and CANCELS 222 (containment).
  - Positive control: a transient queued gap (jobs go 0 → 1) does NOT trip the guard; run completes success.

Let me look at the existing test file structure for where to add — the #34 group (lines ~362-450). Let me view the exact region around the self-heal tests to place the new tests and check the stub `view` branch to mirror the pattern for a `jobs` fixture.

The stub `view` branch currently:
``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/canceled-\$id" ]; then
         status=completed; conclusion=cancelled
       else
         f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
         line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
         sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
         if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
         status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
       fi
       printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
       ;;
``

The script calls `gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion --jq ...`. With `--json jobs`, sub=$2... wait: `cmd="run"; sub="view"`, then `id="$3"` — for `gh run view 111 --repo ... --json jobs --jq ...`, $3=111 too. So the same branch handles it; I need to distinguish by whether "--json jobs" is in args. The stub already collects args into an array and finds --jq. I'll add: if args contain `--json` followed by `jobs`, then serve from jobs-<id>.txt with the same consume-a-line pattern, defaulting to "1" if no file; emit `{"jobs":[{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"queued"}]}`-ish... simplest: emit N in_progress jobs: running count N → `{"jobs":[...N×{"status":"in_progress"}]}`. jq in script: `[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length` → returns N.

Careful with the `cancelled-<id>` marker for the jobs call: after cancel, script has already left the loop; but for cleanliness, serve 0 running jobs when cancelled marker exists (a cancelled run has no running jobs). Actually for the containment test I assert `run cancel 222` in the log — after exit the script doesn't poll again. Fine either way; I'll still make cancelled → 0.

Implementation of the stub branch (careful escaping in the Dart raw string — the stub is inside a Dart string literal with \$ escapes):

``
     view)
       id="\$3"
       is_jobs=0
       for ((j=0; j<\${#args[@]}; j++)); do
         if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ] && [ "\${args[\$((j+1))]}" = "jobs" ]; then is_jobs=1; fi
       done

             if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
           else
             n=1
           fi
         fi
         seq_out="[\`" -- hmm, build array of N in_progress
``

Building the JSON for N jobs in bash: 
``
json="["; k=0; while [ "$k" -lt "$n" ]; do [ "$k" -gt 0 ] && json="$json,"; json="$json{\"status\":\"in_progress\"}"; k=$((k+1)); done; json="$json]"
printf '{"jobs":%s}' "$json" | apply_jq
``
Note: inside the Dart string, `\$` etc. Also `seq` could do: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n"`... seq with -s puts separator between. `seq -s, 1 0` gives... for n=0, `seq 1 0` outputs nothing → json="[]" — but with the -f format: `seq -f ... -s, 1 0` → empty. That's compact:
``
body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)
printf '{"jobs":[%s]}' "\$body" | apply_jq
``
seq -s, 1 3 → `{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"},{"status":"in_progress"}`. For n=0 → empty → `[]`. 

Now the new tests. Also keep `view-111.txt` etc. The repro test:

```dart
test(
 'gh-172: a pool-held child (alive but nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, then fails fast and cancels the orphan',
 () {
   final dw = runDw(
     'queue-stall',
     [
       'build-mobile.yml',
       '--title',
       testflightTitle,
       '--budget-seconds',
       '600', // big: ONLY the queue-stall guard can end attempt 1
       '-f',
       'ios_content=all',
     ],
     {
       'runs.json': runJson([run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10))]),
       'runs2.json': runJson([
         run(111, testflightTitle, iso(-10)),
         run(222, testflightTitle, iso(-1)),
       ]),
       'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       'view-222.txt': 'in_progress -\n',
       // version done, build-ios queued forever: nothing in_progress.
       'jobs-111.txt': '0\n',
       'jobs-222.txt': '0\n',
     },
     env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '1', 'DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS': '1'},
   );
   expect(dw.exitCode, 1);
   expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 2);
   expect(dw.out, contains('runner pool suspect'));
   expect(dw.out, contains('222'));
   expect(
     dw.log.any((l) => l.contains('run cancel 222 --repo OWNER/REPO')),
     reason: 'the orphaned second run must be cancelled before the fail-fast exit',
   );
   expect(dw.out, contains('no running job') /* the stall signature */);
 },
);
``

Wait — one wrinkle: in runDw, DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS default is already '1'. And DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 → tight spin loop; the stall window (1s) fires after ~1s of polls. OK. But note the stall guard must consume polls — with sleep 0 the loop spins hot for 1s; that's fine (existing budget test with budget 1 does the same).

Positive control:

```dart
test('a transient queued gap (job pickup) does not trip the stall guard', () {
 final dw = runDw(
   'queue-transient',
   ['build-mobile.yml', '--title', playTitle, '--budget-seconds', '600', '-f', 'android_content=all'],
   {
     'runs.json': runJson([run(111, playTitle, iso(-10))]),
     // One poll sees nothing running (between version and build-ios),
     // then build-ios is running, then the run completes.
     'jobs-111.txt': '0\n1\n',
     'view-111.txt': 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n',
   },
   env: {'DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS': '2'},
 );
 expect(dw.exitCode, 0);
 expect(dw.log.where((l) => l.startsWith('workflow run')).length, 1);
});
``

Hmm — timing: with poll 0, polls happen as fast as gh stub runs (~few ms each). view-111 consumes line 1 (in_progress), jobs consumes '0' → last_progress=t0; next polls: view consumes 'in_progress' again... wait, the second view poll consumes line 2 of view-111 = 'in_progress -'. Then line exhausted → repeat last = 'completed success'?? No — re-read the stub: it takes head -1, deletes it, and if the file becomes empty it rewrites the consumed line. So the file shrinks to the last line and repeats it forever. view-111.txt 'in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n': poll1→in_progress, poll2→in_progress, poll3→completed success (file then holds just that line). jobs-111 '0\n1\n': poll1→0, poll2→1, poll3+→1 forever.

Sequence: p1: view=in_progress, jobs=0 → last_progress=t0 (initialize last_progress at loop start anyway). p2: view=in_progress, jobs=1 → refresh t1. p3: view=completed success → break. Exit 0 with one dispatch. The stall check at p2: now-t0 ≈ ms < 2s. Safe. But what if p1→p2 takes < stall and p2=1 refreshes — yes safe. To make it a REAL test of the guard, the gap must below the window: with DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2 and the '0' gap lasting ~ms, fine.

Hmm, but also I want a test that the stall guard on attempt 1 leads to re-dispatch (self-heal), not immediate failure — covered by the gh-172 test (it asserts 2 dispatches: attempt 1 stalled → re-dispatch → attempt 2 stalled → fail fast).

Where to place: inside the same group as the self-heal tests (`#34 — wedge self-healing...` presumably). Let me read lines 340-362 to see the group header.

blocks.text:
RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

Wait — careful with the second-atempt message shape. Existing test asserts out contains 'runner pool suspect' and '222' — my message keeps both ('runner pool suspect (issue #34)'). And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

3. Also worth documenting the knob in the usage/env comment block at the top of the script: `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600)`.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic. 

5. While in the yml — no changes to budgets/ceilings (the #351 table must stay in sync with the test).

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

Message wording — keep the signature phrase 'no running job' (test asserts it):
- warning (attempt 1): `::warning::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie) — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- error (attempt 2): `::error::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34, gh-172); URL`

Hmm — to avoid duplicating, keep the wedge string as the cause phrase: wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 zombie-pool signature)" and wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s". Then:
- attempt1: `::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1722 [daily-publish] TestFlight leg failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no
diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run sat `queued` forever on a
zombie-held self-hosted runner — the watcher has no guard for "child run
alive but no job actually running".

**Root cause** (timeline correlated from run
[39374894901](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39374894901)):

1. 05:27:18 — child #1 dispatched (run 39374977270, `build-mobile (none/all)`).
   `Build iOS IPA` starts 05:28:04 on the single self-hosted macOS runner
   `fa-m5-1` and hangs (worker stops reporting — no step logs survive, API
   returns an empty steps array). Its own `timeout-minutes: 90` NEVER fires:
   job-level timeouts on self-hosted runners are enforced by the runner
   process itself, and this worker is exactly the hung-worker class issue #344
   describes. The job runs 250m (05:28:04 → 09:38:29).
2. 09:38:30 — the watcher's budget self-heal (15000s = 250m) fires on schedule:
   `gh run cancel` marks run #1 cancelled server-side. But the physical worker
   never processes the cancellation (the same hung process that ignored its
   90m ceiling) — the runner slot is freed in GitHub's scheduler database
   only when the runner reports; it never reports.
3. 09:39:31 — the watcher re-dispatches child #2 (run 39402285750) per the
   one-shot self-heal design. `Derive version` completes 09:40:18, then
   `Build iOS IPA` goes `queued` at 09:40:18 — **and is still queued now
   (12:01 UTC)**: the zombie worker still holds the single-runner pool, so
   the queued child can never start.
4. 11:27:25 — the leg hits its 360m `timeout-minutes` ceiling and GitHub kills
   the watcher mid-`sleep`. The status-only watch loop
   (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`) saw `in_progress` the whole time — it
   polls run status, never job status — so no wedge was detected, no
   diagnostic was emitted ("no failed-step log available" in the auto-filed
   ticket), and child #2 was left orphaned in the queue (it would start and
   publish unattended hours later if ops revived the runner).

**Impact**: Any wedge of the self-hosted macOS worker turns into a silent
360m ceiling kill: ~107m of leg time burned watching a child that can never
start, no actionable log, an orphaned queued child run left to publish
unattended on pool revival, and an auto-filed issue with zero signal. Affects
every dispatching leg (testflight, play, cli, website, addin) — they share
`dispatch_and_watch.sh`.

**Fix approach** (in `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, the only in-repo lever —
the hung physical worker itself is ops, and the 90m job ceiling that should
have contained it is unenforceable against a dead worker):

- Add a **job-level liveness (queue-stall) guard** to the watch loop: while
  the run is not completed, also poll its jobs; a run with NO job in
  `in_progress` for a bounded window (`DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS`, default 600s —
  healthy children assign/start their first job in seconds) is the
  zombie-pool signature. It feeds the SAME one-shot self-heal path as the
  budget wedge (cancel + re-dispatch once; on the second attempt fail fast).
- **Contain the orphan**: `gh run cancel` the child before the fail-fast exit
  so a server-side-cancelled run can never start/publish unattended when the
  pool revives.

Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg ceiling (~275m: budget
250m + re-dispatch ~13m + stall window 10m) instead of a bare timeout kill at
360m.

**Previous attempt**: n/a — first return of this leg failure shape.
"}

blocks.text:
RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

Wait — careful with the second-atempt message shape. Existing test asserts out contains 'runner pool suspect' and '222' — my message keeps both ('runner pool suspect (issue #34)'). And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

3. Also worth documenting the knob in the usage/env comment block at the top of the script: `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600)`.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic. 

5. While in the yml — no changes to budgets/ceilings (the #351 table must stay in sync with the test).

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

Message wording — keep the signature phrase 'no running job' (test asserts it):
- warning (attempt 1): `::warning::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie) — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- error (attempt 2): `::error::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34, gh-172); URL`

- attempt1: `::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`

Test asserts out contains 'no running job' ✓ and 'runner pool suspect' ✓.

The script calls `gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion --jq ...`. With `--json jobs`, sub=$2... wait: `cmd="run"; sub="view"`, then `id="$3"` — for `gh run view 111 --repo ... --json jobs --jq ...`, $3=111 too. Careful with the `cancelled-<id>` marker for the jobs call: after cancel, script has already left the loop; but for cleanliness, serve 0 running jobs when cancelled marker exists (a cancelled run has no running jobs). RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic.

messages.preview: RED is clean: the old script rides the budget path, never detects the stall, never cancels the orphan run. Now GREEN — implement the queue-stall guard in the watcher:

blocks.text:
RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

Wait — careful with the second-atempt message shape. Existing test asserts out contains 'runner pool suspect' and '222' — my message keeps both ('runner pool suspect (issue #34)'). And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

3. Also worth documenting the knob in the usage/env comment block at the top of the script: `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600)`.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic. 

5. While in the yml — no changes to budgets/ceilings (the #351 table must stay in sync with the test).

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

Message wording — keep the signature phrase 'no running job' (test asserts it):
- warning (attempt 1): `::warning::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie) — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- error (attempt 2): `::error::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34, gh-172); URL`

Hmm — to avoid duplicating, keep the wedge string as the cause phrase: wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 zombie-pool signature)" and wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s". Then:
- attempt1: `::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- attempt2: `::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL`

Test asserts out contains 'no running job' ✓ and 'runner pool suspect' ✓.

Let me now write the script changes.
RED is clean: the old script rides the budget path, never detects the stall, never cancels the orphan run. Now GREEN — implement the queue-stall guard in the watcher:

{"newText":"  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \

        exit 1

      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"

```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

{"newText":"  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi

        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours

blocks.text:
RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

Wait — careful with the second-atempt message shape. Existing test asserts out contains 'runner pool suspect' and '222' — my message keeps both ('runner pool suspect (issue #34)'). And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

3. Also worth documenting the knob in the usage/env comment block at the top of the script: `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600)`.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic.

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

Message wording — keep the signature phrase 'no running job' (test asserts it):
- warning (attempt 1): `::warning::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie) — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`
- error (attempt 2): `::error::$workflow run $run_id no running job for ${queue_stall}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34, gh-172); URL`

- attempt1: `::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); URL`

content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;

RED is now clean and fast: the old script rides the BUDGET path (message "unfinished after 3s"), never sees the queue-stall signature, never emits 'no running job', and exits leaving run 222 uncancelled. The test fails exactly on the missing behaviors. All the other assertions ('runner pool suspect', 2 dispatches, cancel 111) coincidentally pass because the budget path shares them — the distinguishing failures are 'no running job' and 'run cancel 222'.

Now GREEN: implement the fix in scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh.

Design (final):

1. New knob: `queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"`.

2. In the watch loop, after the status poll:
```bash
  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(... status,conclusion ...)
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: ...
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s — pool-held zombie signature (gh-172)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #34 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
      gh run cancel ...
      ... cancel wait ...
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
``

And existing double-wedge fixture (no jobs files → stub default running=1): with the new code, running=1 → refresh → budget path → wedge="unfinished after 1s" → SECOND attempt message unchanged-ish: "build-mobile.yml run 222 unfinished after 1s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); URL". The old message was exactly: "... still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #34); ..." — I dropped the word "still". Keep "still" for continuity: `$wedge` = "still unfinished after ${budget}s" vs "no running job for Xs". Fine.

Also on the fail path, the containment cancel: for the in_progress double-wedge, `gh run cancel 222` — the double-wedge test's stub will then create cancelled-222 marker; no further view calls happen → assertions unaffected. New containment behavior — should the double-wedge test assert it? I'll extend the existing double-wedge test with a cancel-222 expectation... hmm, minimal changes: the gh-172 test asserts cancel-222. For the budget-wedge fail path, the same containment now fires — updating the OLD test to pin it is good practice (it's a behavior change on that path). I'll add the assertion to the double-wedge test.

Hmm wait, actually — should I really cancel on the second-atempt BUDGET path? Think: attempt 2 in_progress-wedged → we exit 1. The run keeps running. If the worker unfreezes, downstream jobs (submit-ios → PUBLISH to TestFlight/Play) execute UNATTENDED at random hours. Cancel marks it dead server-side → no downstream scheduling. This is strictly safer and matches the gh-172 lesson (orphan containment). Yes, keep — one code path for both wedges.

4. Update daily-publish.yml's arithmetic comment: add a line about the gh-172 queue-stall guard so the design note stays truthful ("a second wedge is bounded by the leg timeout" — now: in_progress wedges bounded by leg ceiling; queue-stall wedges fail fast inside the leg). Also the per-leg testflight comment block mentions the same. Minimal touch: extend the shared "Timeout arithmetic" comment block with 2-3 lines. Hmm — also the testflight leg's step comment "Budget 250m = ..." — no change needed there.

Actually — do the leg ceiling numbers need changing? With the stall guard, second-atempt termination happens at budget(250m) + redishpatch(~13m) + stall(10m) ≈ 273m < 360m ✓ for testflight. For cli: budget 350m — attempt 2's stall guard fires at 350m+13m+10m=373m > 360m ceiling... hmm! The cli leg would STILL die at the ceiling for a queued-stall second attempt (ceiling 360). But wait — the cli child (build-macos) — version 20m ubuntu first; the stall window only counts when NOTHING runs. CLI second attempt: dispatch at ~363m?? No wait: attempt 1 budget 350m (15000s? no — cli budget 21000s = 350m) → cancel at ~350m → leg dies at 360m before even the cancel-wait completes. The cli leg's arithmetic is already documented as not fitting two budgets. The stall guard doesn't change that (attempt 1's stall CAN fire early — e.g., cli child queues forever attempt 1: stall at 10m ≪ budget — improvement there). I won't touch cli arithmetic — out of scope; the comment already declares its limitation.

For the testflight leg the guard turns THIS incident (second-atempt queue stall) into a fast diagnostic.

Now — one more edge in the script: `set -euo pipefail` and the `running=$(gh ... ) || running=""` — the `||` protects. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null` under set -e inside an `if` condition is safe.

Another edge: `last_running` must be initialized at watch start (= `started`).

Interplay with budget: I evaluate stall BEFORE budget so the stall wins when both could apply (stall window 600s ≪ budget always in prod). In the elif chain as written: if running>0 → refresh; elif stall-exceeded → stall wedge; elif budget-exceeded → budget wedge. But note: if running==0 and stall not exceeded and budget exceeded → budget wedge ✓. If running=="" (API error) → first two conditions false → budget check still evaluated ✓ (fail-safe).

Wait, one subtle bug in my elif chain: when running>0, `last_running=$now` — then the elifs are skipped (fine). When running==0 and now-last_running>stall → stall. Good.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
